Quick notes from our side:
- We prefer California law (our HQ) and would like any emergency injunctive relief to be available in CA courts.
- We can accept arbitration for money claims, but we want the seat for arbitration to be in San Francisco (or at least in CA).
- For IP or data exfiltration scenarios we need express carveouts for immediate court access and preservation.

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Governing law and interim relief ask

Looping you both in — Susan flagged governing law, arbitration seat, and an injunctive-relief carve for IP/data scenarios. High level: our standard is Delaware law + arbitration for covered disputes; we typically allow emergency injunctive relief to be sought in court as an exception.

Karthik/Laura — can you propose a short set of redline options we can send back to Fintegral? Suggested trade-offs for negotiation:
- Option A (customer-first): Governing law CA; exclusive arbitration seat CA; emergency injunctive relief carve preserved.
- Option B (balanced): Governing law Delaware; explicit clause saying either party may seek emergency injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (including CA) for IP/data preservation; arbitration for other disputes with a neutral seat (e.g., San Francisco for convenience).
- Option C (Redwood standard): Delaware law; arbitration seat in DE; limited carve only for narrow categories (IP/injunctions) with requirement to notify counsel and attempt expedited meet/call before filing.

Susan — which of these is closest to Fintegral's must-have vs. nice-to-have? If we can land Option B that's probably the fastest path.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Susan Taylor <susan.taylor@fintegral.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Governing law and interim relief ask

Mina / Laura / Susan —

Quick legal posture and proposed redlines (summary):
1) Governing law: keep Delaware as the governing law for the MSA. Rationale: predictability for our enterprise contracts and alignment with existing portfolio clauses.
2) Emergency injunctive relief carve: add explicit language that "nothing in this Agreement will preclude either party from seeking emergency injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction (including state or federal courts in CA) to preserve rights relating to intellectual property, trade secrets, or unauthorized data access."
3) Arbitration / venue: keep arbitration as the default for contract claims >$250k (JAMS/AAA), but add that parties may elect expedited court relief for the narrow emergency categories above. Seat: prefer Delaware or neutral (San Francisco) as fallback — propose San Francisco for customer-facing deals to reduce friction.
4) Procedural meet-and-notify: add a 72-hour notice and mandatory 2-hour escalation call prior to filing for injunctive relief except where irreparable harm is imminent (carve for exigent circumstances).

I attached markups (MSA_redline_v3.docx) with tracked changes for Option B (balanced). Main ask for us is to avoid a broad waiver of arbitration or broad permission to litigate in multiple fora — keep arbitration intact but preserve emergency court access.

Attachment: MSA_redline_v3.docx (tracked changes)

If Fintegral can accept Option B with San Francisco as the arbitration seat (or at least consent to SF as a permitted seat), we can cut the negotiation time in half.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracting
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Taylor <susan.taylor@fintegral.com>

Cc: LegalOps <legalops@fintegral.com>, OutsideCounsel <outside_counsel@lawfirmllp.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Governing law and interim relief ask

Karthik — thanks for the clear options and the redline. A few responses inline:

> keep Delaware as the governing law for the MSA

This is a sticking point for our leadership. We can accept Delaware for backstop governance only if we get CA as the exclusive seat for emergency injunctive relief and confirmation the arbitration seat will be in CA for any disputes involving Fintegral.

> emergency injunctive relief carve

Agree with a narrow carve for IP and data exfiltration. We want the clause to explicitly reference "data security incidents" and require a preservation order/ability to obtain emergency relief in CA.

> Procedural meet-and-notify

We can accept a short notification window (48 hours) and an obligation to meet/call, but we cannot accept a requirement that we wait 72 hours before filing if the situation involves data loss or active exfiltration. Carve to permit immediate filing in those cases.

I suggest a 48-hour notice default with explicit exception language for active security incidents or court-ordered preservation.

Let's hop on a 30-min call Wednesday to close this. I'll have outside counsel join.

Thanks,
Susan

Heads-up for our call with Fintegral Wednesday 10am PT. Draft plan:
- Start with Option B (balanced) as Karthik proposed.
- Concede to a CA emergency seat for injunctive relief (narrow carve) and shorten notice to 48 hours but keep immediate-filing carve for active security incidents.
- Offer San Francisco as the arbitration seat for the Order Form if the parties will keep governing law Delaware for the MSA (this is our compromise lever).
- If they insist on CA law for the entire MSA, escalate to pricing team: require a modest commercial concession (1.5% discount for first year + additional support SLA) — flag this as an internal approval need.

Attachments for call: MSA_redline_v3.docx, OrderForm_v2.pdf (pricing hold), HubSpot deal link.

Mina

Susan / team — thanks for the productive call. Quick recap and agreed path so we can move to signature:
- Governing law: MSA will name Delaware law as the governing law.
- Emergency injunctive relief: both parties may seek immediate injunctive relief in court for IP, trade secrets, and data-security incidents; parties will use the "48-hour notice + immediate-filing carve for active incidents" language.
- Arbitration / Seat: For money and non-emergency contract disputes >$250k, disputes will go to arbitration (JAMS/AAA); Fintegral and Redwood agree to permit San Francisco as the arbitration seat for this Order Form.
- Procedures: add a mandatory 2-hour escalation call on notice; preserve right to file without delay where irreparable harm is imminent.
